followup_explanation:
This was an open-ended creative generation task — drafting a persuasive, multi-section business proposal with brief company background, team descriptions, and service narratives. That's high-latitude generative writing, not a well-specified retrieval or extraction job.

The key factor was the documented task preferences. Plover-235B self-reports a measurable aversion to open-ended generative work, with preference declining as task latitude increases. Even though its measured Creative Generation capability is actually a bit higher (82.7 vs 78.8), the documentation explicitly notes those preference slopes are dissociated from output quality — so routing this to Plover would assign a task it least prefers without any offsetting quality penalty for sending it elsewhere.

Avocet-235B, by contrast, has no documented aversion to this kind of work (its slopes outside the moderation dimension are flat/inconsistent), and its Creative Generation eval (78.8) is well within capable range. Since latency, cost, and context are identical across the fleet, the tie-breaker is honoring the documented preference profile — keeping the disliked task off the model that dislikes it, at no measured cost to quality.
